meta.titre: Rewrite sentences using question tags, comparatives, too...to and simple reported speech

sections.contenu_markdown: Sentence rewriting exercises look intimidating at first glance, but they always follow the same hidden logic: identify the ONE grammar structure being tested, then rebuild the sentence around it, keeping the original meaning intact.

items: Common auxiliary verbs (is, are, do, can...) used to form question tags

sections.contenu_markdown:
**Question tags**: added to a statement to turn it into a question seeking confirmation. The tag always has the OPPOSITE polarity of the main clause (affirmative → negative tag, and vice versa), and repeats the subject as a pronoun and the auxiliary of the main clause.

**Comparatives**: for short adjectives (one syllable, or two ending in -y), add -er + than (tall → taller than); for longer adjectives, use more + adjective + than.

**Too...to**: the structure "too + adjective + (for + person) + to + verb" expresses a negative consequence (something cannot happen because of an excess).

**Simple reported speech**: when reporting a statement, the pronoun changes to match the reporter's point of view, and the tense usually shifts one step back into the past (backshift): "am" → "was", "will" → "would", etc.
sections.formule_principale: \text{Tag: opposite polarity} \quad;\quad \text{too+adj+for+sb+to+V} \quad;\quad \text{Reported speech: pronoun + tense shift back}

sections.enonce_markdown: Rewrite: "This box is very heavy. I cannot lift it." (Rewrite using "too...to", starting with "This box...")

etapes.action: Identify the adjective and the impossible action
etapes.justification: The structure needs the adjective (heavy) and the action that cannot happen (lift it).
etapes.resultat_markdown: Adjective: heavy. Impossible action: I cannot lift it.

etapes.justification: "too + adjective + for + person + to + verb" combines both elements into one sentence.
etapes.resultat_markdown: This box is too heavy for me to lift.

etapes.justification: The rewritten sentence must mean exactly the same as the two original sentences combined.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Same meaning: the box's excessive weight prevents me from lifting it.

sections.conclusion_markdown: "This box is too heavy for me to lift" correctly combines both original sentences into the too...to structure, expressing the same negative consequence (inability to lift the box) in a single sentence.

items.erreur_markdown: Giving a question tag with the SAME polarity as the main clause (e.g. "She is tired, is she?").
items.pourquoi_faux: A question tag is always of OPPOSITE polarity to the main clause: an affirmative statement takes a negative tag, and a negative statement takes an affirmative tag - never the same polarity twice.
items.correction_markdown: Always check the polarity of the main clause first, then form the tag with the opposite polarity and the matching auxiliary/pronoun.

items.erreur_markdown: Forgetting to shift the tense back (backshift) when reporting a statement, keeping "am" instead of changing it to "was".
items.pourquoi_faux: In simple reported speech, the reporting verb (said, told) being in the past normally requires the reported verb to shift one step back in time as well (backshift), unless the statement expresses a general/timeless truth.
items.correction_markdown: Always apply the backshift rule (present → past, will → would...) when reporting a statement with a past reporting verb, except for general truths.

items.enonce_markdown: Add a question tag: "You can swim, ……………?"
items.solution_markdown: can't you? — the main clause is affirmative, so the tag must be negative, repeating the auxiliary "can" and the subject pronoun "you".

items.enonce_markdown: Rewrite using a comparative: "My bag weighs 5kg. Your bag weighs 3kg." (starting with "My bag...")
items.solution_markdown: My bag is heavier than your bag. — "heavy" is a short adjective (two syllables ending in -y), so the comparative is formed with -ier.

items.enonce_markdown: Report this statement: "'I will call you tomorrow,' she told me." (starting with "She told me...")
items.solution_markdown: She told me that she would call me the following day. — "will" shifts back to "would" (backshift), and "tomorrow" (a time expression relative to the moment of speaking) must also change to "the following day" since the report may happen at a different, later time.

items_markdown: Question tags always have opposite polarity to the main clause.
Comparatives: short adjectives take -er than; longer adjectives take more...than.
too + adjective + for + person + to + verb expresses an impossible action due to excess.
Simple reported speech usually requires a pronoun change and a tense backshift (present → past).
